title: Supabase local stack: config.toml, pg_cron/pgmq/pg_net extensions, asymmetric JWT signing keys, lifecycle scripts
objective: Stand up the reproducible local Supabase development stack (database, auth, storage, studio) via Supabase CLI + Docker so that a clean checkout can run supabase start and obtain a working local platform including Auth with asymmetric JWT signing keys and the pg_cron, pgmq, and pg_net extensions (M-19, A-4, A-10, Q-7).
scope: supabase/config.toml: project config for local stack — auth enabled (email/password), site URL + additional redirect URLs for the SPA password-reset flow, storage enabled, studio enabled; asymmetric JWT signing keys enabled locally per A-10

Ensure pg_cron, pgmq, and pg_net are available/enabled in the local stack (config plus a first extensions migration if needed here or deferred to T-003 — decide and document; the extensions must exist before T-003 migrations apply)
Lifecycle scripts wired for real: supabase:start, supabase:stop, supabase:reset (supabase db reset), db:migrate (supabase db push / migration up against local)
.env.local.example updated with the local-stack values shape (VITE_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321, anon key + service-role key placeholders as printed by supabase start)
docs/local-development.md first real content: prerequisites (Docker, Supabase CLI), start/stop/reset commands, where local keys come from
out_of_scope: Hosted Supabase project provisioning (human-owned, deferred per A-18)
implementation_details: supabase init if no supabase/ directory exists; pin CLI expectations in docs (minimum CLI version that supports asymmetric signing keys and pgmq locally).

config.toml [auth]: enable email provider, disable signups if the product provisions users only via Auth Admin API (User Manager) — verify against P-01/P-03 and set accordingly; configure site_url http://localhost:5173 (Vite dev) and additional_redirect_urls for the reset flow.
Asymmetric JWT signing keys: configure the local stack so auth.getClaims() verifies against JWKS offline (A-10). Document the verification expectation for tests.

Extensions: prefer enabling via the first SQL migration (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_cron/pgmq/pg_net...) so hosted environments get them through the same migration path; config.toml only where the local stack needs it. Coordinate with T-003 so ordering is deterministic.
supabase:reset script must run migrations + seed.sql hook (seed content arrives in T-006).
Verify supabase start works from clean checkout on Windows (Docker Desktop) — document any platform caveats.

integration: From clean checkout: supabase start succeeds; supabase db reset succeeds with zero migrations or the extensions migration only
psql/SQL check: pg_cron, pgmq, pg_net extensions installed and usable in the local database

Local Auth: create a throwaway user via the Auth Admin API with the printed service-role key; sign in with password; verify the issued access token validates against the local JWKS (asymmetric keys active)

findings.description: V-004 expected result #1 requires that health of the database, auth (GoTrue), AND storage services is asserted (HTTP/DB probes). The T-002 integration suites probe the database (direct SQL via pg) and auth (Admin API provisioning, sign-in, JWKS, getClaims) but contain no storage health assertion anywhere. probeLocalStack() only parses `supabase status -o json` for API_URL/DB_URL/keys, and `supabase status` exits 0 even when individual services are stopped (it merely lists them under 'Stopped services'). Consequence: if [storage] were disabled in config.toml (exactly as was deliberately done for realtime/analytics/edge_runtime) or the storage container were dead, every T-002 test would still pass - a false-green path of the class this repo has been bitten by twice. Evaluator manually confirmed storage IS healthy today (GET /storage/v1/version -> 200 '1.62.5'; docker ps shows supabase_storage_quoteiq Up (healthy)), so this is a missing regression assertion, not a broken stack.
findings.evidence: src/server/tests/integration/local-stack-extensions.test.ts and local-stack-auth.test.ts: no reference to /storage. src/server/tests/integration/helpers/local-stack.ts probeLocalStack() checks only API_URL/DB_URL/ANON_KEY/SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. Evaluator probe: GET http://127.0.0.1:54321/storage/v1/version -> HTTP 200 body '1.62.5'; `supabase status` exited 0 while listing 6 stopped services, proving stopped services do not fail the probe.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one HTTP-probe test to a T-002 integration suite (or a small local-stack-services.test.ts) asserting storage health via the running stack, e.g. GET `${stack.apiUrl}/storage/v1/version` returns 200 with a non-empty version string (optionally also GET /auth/v1/health -> 200 for symmetry). Reuse probeLocalStack()/suiteTitle() so the skip-visibility behavior is preserved.
findings.resolution: Added src/server/tests/integration/local-stack-storage.test.ts (2 tests) closing the V-004 storage-health gap: GET {apiUrl}/storage/v1/version must return 200 with non-empty body, and the service-role bucket API must return a JSON array. Uses the existing probeLocalStack()/suiteTitle() helpers so the Docker-unavailable skip stays visible. PROVEN NON-HOLLOW: with supabase_storage_quoteiq stopped, both tests FAIL (exit 1); container restarted and suite green again. Also added AbortSignal.timeout(10s) because the down-container case otherwise hung ~54s on OS connection timeout, which would stall CI on exactly the failure this suite exists to catch. Verified: npm test 10 files / 108 tests passed (was 9/106), typecheck 0, lint 0.
findings.summary: V-004 expected result #1 requires that health of the database, auth (GoTrue), AND storage services is asserted (HTTP/DB probes).

Orchestrator resolved F-002-1 directly (single additive test, no Implementor delegation needed). Storage health now asserted; non-hollowness proven by stopping the storage container and observing both tests fail, then restarting. Fast-fail timeout added. Status IMPLEMENTED, returned to Evaluator for iteration 1 re-review.

Evaluator iteration 1 re-review: PASS. F-002-1 confirmed genuinely closed - evaluator independently re-proved non-hollowness by stopping supabase_storage_quoteiq: both storage tests FAIL (exit 1) via AbortSignal timeout at ~10s each (not the ~54s OS hang), then restarted the container (healthy after 10s, /storage/v1/version -> 200 '1.62.5' in ~4.5ms). The probe cannot be satisfied by a stack with [storage] disabled in config.toml: the /version test asserts HTTP 200 + non-empty body and the bucket test asserts a service-role-authenticated JSON array, neither of which a missing upstream can produce through Kong. Skip-visibility contract honoured: the new suite reuses probeLocalStack()/suiteTitle() identically to the two existing suites (stderr [SKIPPED] line + reason folded into suite title + changed reporter counts), verified by code inspection against the mechanism empirically proven in iteration 1. 10s timeout judged ADEQUATE, no raise needed: healthy-stack responses measured ~5ms (>1000x margin), the suite only runs after probeLocalStack() confirms `supabase status` healthy (which itself gates on stack readiness), and vitest testTimeout empirically exceeds 10s so the abort - not the runner - is the failure mechanism. Full re-run with stack healthy: npm test 10 files / 108 tests passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (exit 0, exit codes captured directly, no pipes); typecheck exit 0; lint exit 0; stub db:seed exits 1 loudly. Regression spot-checks intact: signing_keys.json still git-ignored in supabase/.gitignore; [auth].enable_signup=false with [auth.email].enable_signup=true still pinned in config.toml; .env.local.example still placeholder-only (no JWT/secret material). ES256/JWKS offline verification and extensions coverage re-confirmed via the 108-test green run (0 skipped proves integration suites executed against the live stack). V-004 satisfied; V-115 (AC-089, manual) remains UNSATISFIED by design, judged at T-042. Stack left RUNNING and healthy for T-003 (all 8 containers Up, storage healthy).

SIGNUP POLICY: [auth].enable_signup = false (no self-service registration; identities come only from the Auth Admin API per P-01/P-03). [auth.email].enable_signup MUST remain true - it maps to GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_EMAIL_ENABLED and setting it false also rejects sign-in with 'Email logins are disabled'. Discovered by test failure; both halves now pinned by a regression test.

JWT KEYS: [auth].signing_keys_path = ./signing_keys.json, ES256 key generated per machine by scripts/db/ensure-signing-keys.mjs and git-ignored (it is a private key). Confirmed tokens are ES256 with a kid, JWKS exposes public EC keys only, and signatures verify offline via both raw WebCrypto and auth.getClaims().

notes: Windows/Node caveat: Node 22+ refuses to spawn npx.cmd without a shell (EINVAL). Repository scripts and the test helper invoke the CLI's JS entrypoint with process.execPath instead. Documented in docs/local-development.md.

CLI 2.109.1 quirk: `supabase gen signing-key` READS signing_keys_path before writing and aborts with LegacyGenSigningKeyReadError if absent. The script seeds '[]' then uses --append, and validates the result is a non-empty ES256 key set.

Integration suites skip cleanly (no hang) when the stack is down, and the skip reason is written to stderr AND folded into the suite title, because a silently skipped suite is indistinguishable from a passing one. CI (T-010) must additionally assert the stack is up.

V-115 (AC-089) remains UNSATISFIED by design: docs/local-development.md cannot yet cover seeded sign-in credentials (T-006/T-041), running backend + SPA (T-009/T-018), or the e2e suite (T-043). Judged at T-042.
